person.name: Thomas_Jefferson
person.summary: Thomas Jefferson was a Virginia lawyer, planter, political writer, diplomat, and the third president of the United States. He drafted the Declaration of Independence, led the Louisiana Purchase, sent the Corps of Discovery westward, and founded the University of Virginia. He also enslaved more than 600 people during his life, including people at Monticello.

conclusion: Thomas Jefferson's Declaration of Independence remains a central text of United States civic life and is read by students, courts, public officials, and political movements. The Louisiana Purchase and the Lewis and Clark Expedition expanded United States claims across the continent and supplied maps, specimens, and records used by later settlers, scientists, and government officials. The University of Virginia continues to operate in Charlottesville, where its academic village follows Jefferson's architectural plan.

events.title: Born at Shadwell
events.description: Thomas Jefferson was born into the Shadwell plantation household of Peter Jefferson and Jane Randolph in the Virginia colony. Peter Jefferson worked as a planter and surveyor. Thomas was the third of their ten children.

events.title: Enters William and Mary
events.description: Thomas Jefferson entered the College of William & Mary in Williamsburg in 1761. Professor William Small taught him mathematics and philosophy. Small introduced him to [[Enlightenment|Enlightenment ideas]] and to George Wythe and Governor Francis Fauquier.

images.caption: Wren Building, College of William and Mary
images.creator: Ken Lund

Enlightenment.explanation: The Enlightenment was an intellectual movement that emphasized reason, empirical inquiry, and criticism of traditional authority. Its ideas influenced Jefferson's studies and later political thought.

events.title: Begins Legal Career
events.description: Thomas Jefferson began practicing law in Virginia in 1767. He had read law under George Wythe, a leading Virginia lawyer and legislator. His legal work gave him a profession before his entry into colonial politics.

images.caption: Interior of the George Wythe House, Williamsburg
images.creator: Unknown authorUnknown author

events.background:
Jefferson lived with his mother at Shadwell while establishing his practice. In 1767, he handled 68 cases before Virginia's General Court. His work there later included Howell v. Netherland, Bolling v. Bolling, and Blair v. Blair.

His practice included seven enslaved clients seeking freedom. He waived his fee for one client and argued that the man had a natural right to control his own person. The judge stopped the argument and ruled against the client. Jefferson gave the man money afterward.

From 1769 through 1775, Jefferson also represented Albemarle County in the House of Burgesses. He sponsored a measure to give enslavers discretion to emancipate people without approval from the royal governor or courts. Richard Bland led the bill's effort in the legislature. It faced strong opposition in Virginia's agrarian economy.

background_images.creator: Frances Benjamin Johnston

events.title: Marries Martha Wayles
events.description: Thomas Jefferson married Martha Wayles Skelton near Williamsburg on January 1, 1772. Martha was a widowed planter’s daughter. They made their home at [[Monticello|Monticello]], Jefferson’s plantation residence near Charlottesville.

Monticello.explanation: Monticello was Jefferson’s plantation estate near Charlottesville, Virginia, which he began constructing in 1768. The couple made it their principal household after marrying.

events.title: Drafts the Declaration of Independence
events.description: Thomas Jefferson drafted the Declaration of Independence in Philadelphia for the Committee of Five. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Robert R. Livingston, and Roger Sherman served with him on the committee. The Second Continental Congress revised the text and adopted it on July 4, 1776. The Pennsylvania Evening Post printed it two days later.

event_class.title: Declaration of Independence
event_class.impact: The Continental Congress adopts the declaration as the public statement of the thirteen colonies' independence from Great Britain.

events.background:
Fighting had begun at Lexington and Concord the previous year, and Congress had come to favor a formal break with Britain. The committee first considered having Adams prepare the text. Adams urged the choice of Jefferson because he was a Virginian, popular, and an able writer. Jefferson consulted the other members of the committee. He wrote most of the draft in isolation between June 11 and June 28. He drew on his proposed Virginia Constitution, George Mason’s draft of the Virginia Declaration of Rights, and other sources.

The committee altered the draft before submitting it to Congress on June 28. Congress began debating it on July 1 and removed roughly one-quarter of Jefferson’s original wording. Jefferson resented the changes. He made no public objection. The delegates did not sign until August 2. They understood that the Crown could prosecute them for high treason, which carried the threat of torture and death. The text received its first simultaneous public readings on July 8 in Trenton, Easton, and Philadelphia.

events.title: Governs Wartime Virginia
events.description: Thomas Jefferson served as Virginia’s governor during the American Revolutionary War. The Virginia General Assembly moved the capital from Williamsburg to Richmond during his governorship. British forces under Benedict Arnold forced Jefferson from Richmond in 1781. Jack Jouett warned him that Banastre Tarleton was approaching Monticello, and Jefferson escaped.

events.title: Martha Dies at Monticello
events.description: Martha Wayles Skelton Jefferson died at Monticello on September 6, 1782. Years of ill health and difficult pregnancies had weakened her. Thomas Jefferson was at her bedside. He withdrew in grief and later took long rides with their daughter Martha.

events.title: Leaves for Paris
events.description: Congress sent Thomas Jefferson to Paris to negotiate treaties of amity and commerce for the United States. He sailed from Boston in July 1784 with his daughter Martha Jefferson Randolph and the enslaved James Hemings. They arrived in Paris the following month.

events.title: Becomes Secretary of State
events.description: Thomas Jefferson took office as the first United States secretary of state in Philadelphia in 1790. President George Washington had appointed him the year before. Jefferson managed foreign relations. He clashed with Treasury Secretary Alexander Hamilton over debt, finance, and federal power.
events.background:
The new administration had to settle the permanent location of the national capital while it was still based in Philadelphia. Hamilton wanted a site near the Northeast's commercial centers. Jefferson and other agrarians supported a southern location. The Compromise of 1790 put the capital on the Potomac River. It also brought the Revolutionary War debts of all thirteen original states under the federal government.

Jefferson wanted the states to pay their own debts. He opposed Hamilton's plans to consolidate those debts, create national credit, and establish a national bank. His efforts against Hamilton's program became forceful enough that Washington nearly removed him from the cabinet.

Jefferson also tried to shift American commerce away from Britain and toward France. He sought to reduce Spanish power beyond the Appalachian Mountains and British influence in the North. In talks with British Minister George Hammond, he asked Britain to abandon its posts in the Northwest and compensate the United States for enslaved people freed by British forces at the end of the Revolutionary War. Hammond did not grant either request.

events.title: Serves as Vice President
events.description: Thomas Jefferson took office as vice president under President John Adams on March 4, 1797. He had received the second-highest total in the 1796 presidential election. The electoral rules then made the runner-up vice president. Jefferson also presided over the Senate.

events.title: Takes the Presidency
events.description: Thomas Jefferson took office as the third president of the United States in Washington on March 4, 1801. He had defeated John Adams in the election of 1800. His [[Democratic-Republican Party|Democratic-Republican Party]] formed the administration with Aaron Burr as vice president and James Madison as secretary of state.

images.caption: United States Capitol, completed northern wing
images.creator: Thomas Birch

Democratic-Republican Party.explanation: Jefferson and James Madison organized this political party in 1792 to oppose Federalist policies. It favored a limited federal government and was the forerunner of the modern Democratic Party.

events.title: Purchases Louisiana from France
events.description: Robert R. Livingston and James Monroe signed the Louisiana Purchase agreement with François Barbé-Marbois in Paris on April 30, 1803. Jefferson had sent Livingston and Monroe to negotiate for the United States. France transferred New Orleans and the Louisiana territory to the United States for $15 million.
events.background:
Access to the Mississippi River shaped the negotiations. Farmers west of the Appalachian Mountains relied on the river to move goods to market. The right to store exports at New Orleans had become essential. Spain's temporary withdrawal of that right raised fears about a foreign power controlling the river's outlet. France's recovery of Louisiana from Spain made those fears immediate.

The American representatives had authority to spend up to $10 million on New Orleans and nearby land. Napoleon's government offered the whole territory. France had failed to put down the revolt in Saint-Domingue. Renewed war with the United Kingdom also threatened France. The financial terms set $11.25 million for France and assigned $3.75 million in American claims against France to the United States.

France exercised authority over only a small part of the territory. Native peoples inhabited most of it. The agreement gave the United States a claim to obtain Native lands through later treaties or conquest. Federalists challenged the purchase in Congress. Jefferson and James Madison secured Senate ratification and congressional funding later in 1803.

events.title: Sends Corps of Discovery West
events.description: The Corps of Discovery, an Army expedition led by Meriwether Lewis and William Clark, left Camp Dubois on May 14, 1804. Thomas Jefferson had commissioned the expedition to examine the Louisiana territory acquired from France. Its orders included meeting Native nations along the Missouri River and seeking a route to the Pacific Ocean.

images.caption: Camp Dubois, Lewis and Clark expedition starting point
images.creator: en:User:Americasroof

events.title: Signs Embargo Act
events.description: Thomas Jefferson signed the Embargo Act on December 22, 1807. British interference with American shipping had prompted the measure. The law barred American ships from foreign trade. Jefferson intended it to protect American shipping and encourage domestic manufacturing.

images.caption: British political cartoon ridiculing the Embargo Act
images.creator: Isaac Cruikshank

events.title: Helps Found University of Virginia
events.description: Virginia chartered the University of Virginia in Charlottesville in 1819. The institution grew from the earlier Central College project that Thomas Jefferson had helped create. Jefferson planned its buildings and curriculum for advanced education in Virginia.

images.caption: Rotunda and Lawn, University of Virginia
images.creator: Phil Roeder

events.title: Dies at Monticello
events.description: Thomas Jefferson spent his last years at Monticello with declining health and severe financial strain. His daughter Martha Jefferson Randolph helped care for him there. He was bedridden by 1826. He died on July 4, 1826, the fiftieth anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.
